compliance.reason: Permenhut 6/2026 Pasal 61's transitional filing deadline does not apply — no SRUK/SRN-PPI registration (Pasal 61 doesn't cover the international/Verra track).

other_rules.reason: Pasal 10's Unit Karbon precondition governs the domestic SRUK track; this candidate is on the international/Verra (DPP) track instead.
No land_rights_category on file yet — Pasal 6(1) actor-category eligibility not yet checked (this is 'not yet checked', not a confirmed gap).
Verra/international-track candidate but no DPP registration date on file yet — per Pasal 20(a), pencatatan DPP is the first-step precondition before requesting non-SPE GRK approval.

not_wired_rules.reason: Regulation citation/enactment metadata, not a per-candidate obligation.
The regulation's own effective-date clause, not a per-candidate obligation.

Pasal 6(2) requires legal-standing documentation specific to the Perhutanan Sosial/masyarakat hukum adat/hutan hak categories, beyond simple category membership (which R003 does check) — no such document field exists on UnifiedCandidateRecord.
Pasal 9(1) scopes eligible trading to specific forest-area (kawasan) types; UnifiedCandidateRecord has no normalized kawasan-type field to test against.

Pasal 11-14's 5+5-working-day DRAM review SLA needs the DRAM submission timestamp; the raw `dram` field is a source-schema passthrough with no guaranteed submission-date key across the known SRUK/SRN-PPI schema variants.
Pasal 15-17's 14-working-day SPE GRK recommendation SLA needs the application submission date; not present as a normalized field.
Internal Kementerian document-completeness process between officials — not observable from candidate-side data at all.

Pasal 24's 6-month clock starts at Menteri approval issuance ('persetujuan terbit'), a distinct event from dpp.registration_date (Verra's own registration date) — treating them as the same date would misreport which event actually started the clock.
Pasal 26(3)'s 7-working-day SLA needs the Corresponding Adjustment request date; not present as a normalized field.
Pasal 28's safeguard-principle obligation needs safeguard/audit documentation UnifiedCandidateRecord doesn't capture.

Pasal 41-45's independent LVV validation/verification requirement is specific to the domestic Unit Karbon (SRUK) track; there's no normalized 'validated by LVV' field distinct from the raw `dram` passthrough, and reusing Verra's own verra_status here would conflate the domestic and international tracks.
Pasal 54's reporting obligation has no explicit frequency in the rule text itself ('frekuensi tidak disebutkan eksplisit') — nothing to test a specific date against.
Pasal 55(4) binds the Menteri to run an annual review (pihak_terkait: 'Menteri') — never a per-candidate obligation.
Pasal 63's roadmap deadline binds the Menteri, not individual Pelaku Usaha (pihak_terkait says so explicitly) — never applicable to a candidate.
Repeal clause (revokes Permen LHK 7/2023) — not a per-candidate obligation.
Transitional internal registry-operations procedure binding Kementerian Kehutanan internally, not candidates.

Pasal 18 distinguishes SPE GRK recommendation (Menteri Kehutanan's authority) from final SPE GRK issuance (Menteri LH's authority) — two different ministries in one workflow. registration_stage is a single undifferentiated 1-5 progress integer with no field marking which ministry's action is pending.

Pasal 19 classifies the BUYER/counterparty (compliance market vs voluntary market vs public) for a candidate that already holds SPE GRK — about the transaction's counterparty, not the candidate's own registration state. UnifiedCandidateRecord profiles project candidates, not trades, and has no buyer/counterparty field.

Twin of R007 for the DPP track (Pasal 21's 5+5-working-day DPP review SLA) — same blocker as R007: needs the DPP submission timestamp, and `dpp` only carries registration_date/crediting_period dates/methodology (see normalize_verra.py), no submission-date field.

Pasal 22 requires FOUR things together (independent DPP validation, implementation per DPP, independent achievement verification, and a verification report) to support a non-SPE GRK approval request. Verra's own validator/verra_units.issued are evidence from Verra's OWN international process (VCS), not Indonesia's Ministry-level Pasal 22 process — a plausibly-related but different jurisdiction's fact, not the same legal fact. That cross-jurisdiction gap is why this stays unscored here; dossier.py's dpp_validation_proxy surfaces it separately as unscored, hypothesis-tagged, dossier-only evidence (never a badge, never a scoring input) rather than losing the signal entirely.

Twin of R008 for the DPP track (Pasal 23's 14-working-day document-completeness review) — same blocker as R008: needs the non-SPE GRK application submission date, not a normalized field. (Its resulting approval's validity period is governed by R010, already flagged for the same Menteri-approval-date gap.)

not_wired_rules.reason: Regulation citation/enactment metadata, not a per-candidate obligation.
The regulation's own effective-date clause, not a per-candidate obligation.

Pasal 6(2) requires legal-standing documentation specific to the Perhutanan Sosial/masyarakat hukum adat/hutan hak categories, beyond simple category membership (which R003 does check) — no such document field exists on UnifiedCandidateRecord.
Pasal 9(1) scopes eligible trading to specific forest-area (kawasan) types; UnifiedCandidateRecord has no normalized kawasan-type field to test against.

Pasal 11-14's 5+5-working-day DRAM review SLA needs the DRAM submission timestamp; the raw `dram` field is a source-schema passthrough with no guaranteed submission-date key across the known SRUK/SRN-PPI schema variants.
Pasal 15-17's 14-working-day SPE GRK recommendation SLA needs the application submission date; not present as a normalized field.
Internal Kementerian document-completeness process between officials — not observable from candidate-side data at all.

Pasal 26(3)'s 7-working-day SLA needs the Corresponding Adjustment request date; not present as a normalized field.
Pasal 28's safeguard-principle obligation needs safeguard/audit documentation UnifiedCandidateRecord doesn't capture.

not_wired_rules.reason: Regulation citation/enactment metadata, not a per-candidate obligation.
The regulation's own effective-date clause, not a per-candidate obligation.

Pasal 6(2) requires legal-standing documentation specific to the Perhutanan Sosial/masyarakat hukum adat/hutan hak categories, beyond simple category membership (which R003 does check) — no such document field exists on UnifiedCandidateRecord.
Pasal 9(1) scopes eligible trading to specific forest-area (kawasan) types; UnifiedCandidateRecord has no normalized kawasan-type field to test against.

Pasal 11-14's 5+5-working-day DRAM review SLA needs the DRAM submission timestamp; the raw `dram` field is a source-schema passthrough with no guaranteed submission-date key across the known SRUK/SRN-PPI schema variants.
Pasal 15-17's 14-working-day SPE GRK recommendation SLA needs the application submission date; not present as a normalized field.
Internal Kementerian document-completeness process between officials — not observable from candidate-side data at all.

Pasal 24's 6-month clock starts at Menteri approval issuance ('persetujuan terbit'), a distinct event from dpp.registration_date (Verra's own registration date) — treating them as the same date would misreport which event actually started the clock.
Pasal 26(3)'s 7-working-day SLA needs the Corresponding Adjustment request date; not present as a normalized field.
Pasal 28's safeguard-principle obligation needs safeguard/audit documentation UnifiedCandidateRecord doesn't capture.

Pasal 41-45's independent LVV validation/verification requirement is specific to the domestic Unit Karbon (SRUK) track; there's no normalized 'validated by LVV' field distinct from the raw `dram` passthrough, and reusing Verra's own verra_status here would conflate the domestic and international tracks.
Pasal 54's reporting obligation has no explicit frequency in the rule text itself ('frekuensi tidak disebutkan eksplisit') — nothing to test a specific date against.
Pasal 55(4) binds the Menteri to run an annual review (pihak_terkait: 'Menteri') — never a per-candidate obligation.
Pasal 63's roadmap deadline binds the Menteri, not individual Pelaku Usaha (pihak_terkait says so explicitly) — never applicable to a candidate.
Repeal clause (revokes Permen LHK 7/2023) — not a per-candidate obligation.
Transitional internal registry-operations procedure binding Kementerian Kehutanan internally, not candidates.

Pasal 18 distinguishes SPE GRK recommendation (Menteri Kehutanan's authority) from final SPE GRK issuance (Menteri LH's authority) — two different ministries in one workflow. registration_stage is a single undifferentiated 1-5 progress integer with no field marking which ministry's action is pending.

Pasal 19 classifies the BUYER/counterparty (compliance market vs voluntary market vs public) for a candidate that already holds SPE GRK — about the transaction's counterparty, not the candidate's own registration state. UnifiedCandidateRecord profiles project candidates, not trades, and has no buyer/counterparty field.

Twin of R007 for the DPP track (Pasal 21's 5+5-working-day DPP review SLA) — same blocker as R007: needs the DPP submission timestamp, and `dpp` only carries registration_date/crediting_period dates/methodology (see normalize_verra.py), no submission-date field.

Pasal 22 requires FOUR things together (independent DPP validation, implementation per DPP, independent achievement verification, and a verification report) to support a non-SPE GRK approval request. Verra's own validator/verra_units.issued are evidence from Verra's OWN international process (VCS), not Indonesia's Ministry-level Pasal 22 process — a plausibly-related but different jurisdiction's fact, not the same legal fact. That cross-jurisdiction gap is why this stays unscored here; dossier.py's dpp_validation_proxy surfaces it separately as unscored, hypothesis-tagged, dossier-only evidence (never a badge, never a scoring input) rather than losing the signal entirely.

Twin of R008 for the DPP track (Pasal 23's 14-working-day document-completeness review) — same blocker as R008: needs the non-SPE GRK application submission date, not a normalized field. (Its resulting approval's validity period is governed by R010, already flagged for the same Menteri-approval-date gap.)

Transitional internal registry-operations procedure binding Kementerian Kehutanan internally, not candidates.

Dear Hanif Rahman,

Verra status is early-stage (Pipeline listing requested (under development)) with no further progress recorded.

Gluri operates treXchange, a satellite- and AI-based monitoring, reporting, and verification (dMRV) platform for forest-carbon projects. We're reaching out to organizations across Indonesia's forestry-carbon sector to explore whether treXchange could support your project's measurement and verification needs alongside your existing registry process.

Insufficient signal to suggest a specific pilot scope yet — recommend a discovery call first.

A few things it'd help us understand on an initial call:
- What's currently blocking submission of technical/monitoring documentation?
- Do you have a georeferenced project boundary (KML/shapefile) beyond a single point location?
- Is this site within or adjacent to any customary/indigenous (adat) territory?

Best regards,
The Gluri team

-----
Versi Bahasa Indonesia / Indonesian version below
-----

Yth. Hanif Rahman,

Verra status is early-stage (Pipeline listing requested (under development)) with no further progress recorded.

Gluri mengoperasikan treXchange, sebuah platform pemantauan, pelaporan, dan verifikasi (dMRV) berbasis satelit dan AI untuk proyek karbon hutan. Kami menghubungi berbagai organisasi di sektor karbon kehutanan Indonesia untuk menjajaki apakah treXchange dapat mendukung kebutuhan pengukuran dan verifikasi proyek Anda, sejalan dengan proses registrasi yang sudah berjalan.

Insufficient signal to suggest a specific pilot scope yet — recommend a discovery call first.

Beberapa hal yang ingin kami pahami dalam panggilan awal:
- What's currently blocking submission of technical/monitoring documentation?
- Do you have a georeferenced project boundary (KML/shapefile) beyond a single point location?
- Is this site within or adjacent to any customary/indigenous (adat) territory?

Pasal 6(2) requires legal-standing documentation specific to the Perhutanan Sosial/masyarakat hukum adat/hutan hak categories, beyond simple category membership (which R003 does check) — no such document field exists on UnifiedCandidateRecord.
Pasal 9(1) scopes eligible trading to specific forest-area (kawasan) types; UnifiedCandidateRecord has no normalized kawasan-type field to test against.

Pasal 11-14's 5+5-working-day DRAM review SLA needs the DRAM submission timestamp; the raw `dram` field is a source-schema passthrough with no guaranteed submission-date key across the known SRUK/SRN-PPI schema variants.
Pasal 15-17's 14-working-day SPE GRK recommendation SLA needs the application submission date; not present as a normalized field.
Internal Kementerian document-completeness process between officials — not observable from candidate-side data at all.

Pasal 24's 6-month clock starts at Menteri approval issuance ('persetujuan terbit'), a distinct event from dpp.registration_date (Verra's own registration date) — treating them as the same date would misreport which event actually started the clock.
Pasal 26(3)'s 7-working-day SLA needs the Corresponding Adjustment request date; not present as a normalized field.
Pasal 28's safeguard-principle obligation needs safeguard/audit documentation UnifiedCandidateRecord doesn't capture.

Pasal 41-45's independent LVV validation/verification requirement is specific to the domestic Unit Karbon (SRUK) track; there's no normalized 'validated by LVV' field distinct from the raw `dram` passthrough, and reusing Verra's own verra_status here would conflate the domestic and international tracks.
Pasal 54's reporting obligation has no explicit frequency in the rule text itself ('frekuensi tidak disebutkan eksplisit') — nothing to test a specific date against.
Pasal 55(4) binds the Menteri to run an annual review (pihak_terkait: 'Menteri') — never a per-candidate obligation.
Pasal 63's roadmap deadline binds the Menteri, not individual Pelaku Usaha (pihak_terkait says so explicitly) — never applicable to a candidate.
Repeal clause (revokes Permen LHK 7/2023) — not a per-candidate obligation.
Transitional internal registry-operations procedure binding Kementerian Kehutanan internally, not candidates.

Pasal 18 distinguishes SPE GRK recommendation (Menteri Kehutanan's authority) from final SPE GRK issuance (Menteri LH's authority) — two different ministries in one workflow. registration_stage is a single undifferentiated 1-5 progress integer with no field marking which ministry's action is pending.

Pasal 19 classifies the BUYER/counterparty (compliance market vs voluntary market vs public) for a candidate that already holds SPE GRK — about the transaction's counterparty, not the candidate's own registration state. UnifiedCandidateRecord profiles project candidates, not trades, and has no buyer/counterparty field.

Twin of R007 for the DPP track (Pasal 21's 5+5-working-day DPP review SLA) — same blocker as R007: needs the DPP submission timestamp, and `dpp` only carries registration_date/crediting_period dates/methodology (see normalize_verra.py), no submission-date field.

Pasal 22 requires FOUR things together (independent DPP validation, implementation per DPP, independent achievement verification, and a verification report) to support a non-SPE GRK approval request. Verra's own validator/verra_units.issued are evidence from Verra's OWN international process (VCS), not Indonesia's Ministry-level Pasal 22 process — a plausibly-related but different jurisdiction's fact, not the same legal fact. That cross-jurisdiction gap is why this stays unscored here; dossier.py's dpp_validation_proxy surfaces it separately as unscored, hypothesis-tagged, dossier-only evidence (never a badge, never a scoring input) rather than losing the signal entirely.

Twin of R008 for the DPP track (Pasal 23's 14-working-day document-completeness review) — same blocker as R008: needs the non-SPE GRK application submission date, not a normalized field. (Its resulting approval's validity period is governed by R010, already flagged for the same Menteri-approval-date gap.)

other_rules.reason: Pasal 10's Unit Karbon precondition governs the domestic SRUK track; this candidate is on the international/Verra (DPP) track instead.
No land_rights_category on file yet — Pasal 6(1) actor-category eligibility not yet checked (this is 'not yet checked', not a confirmed gap).
Verra/international-track candidate but no DPP registration date on file yet — per Pasal 20(a), pencatatan DPP is the first-step precondition before requesting non-SPE GRK approval.

not_wired_rules.reason: Regulation citation/enactment metadata, not a per-candidate obligation.
The regulation's own effective-date clause, not a per-candidate obligation.

Pasal 6(2) requires legal-standing documentation specific to the Perhutanan Sosial/masyarakat hukum adat/hutan hak categories, beyond simple category membership (which R003 does check) — no such document field exists on UnifiedCandidateRecord.
Pasal 9(1) scopes eligible trading to specific forest-area (kawasan) types; UnifiedCandidateRecord has no normalized kawasan-type field to test against.

Pasal 11-14's 5+5-working-day DRAM review SLA needs the DRAM submission timestamp; the raw `dram` field is a source-schema passthrough with no guaranteed submission-date key across the known SRUK/SRN-PPI schema variants.
Pasal 15-17's 14-working-day SPE GRK recommendation SLA needs the application submission date; not present as a normalized field.
Internal Kementerian document-completeness process between officials — not observable from candidate-side data at all.

Pasal 24's 6-month clock starts at Menteri approval issuance ('persetujuan terbit'), a distinct event from dpp.registration_date (Verra's own registration date) — treating them as the same date would misreport which event actually started the clock.
Pasal 26(3)'s 7-working-day SLA needs the Corresponding Adjustment request date; not present as a normalized field.
Pasal 28's safeguard-principle obligation needs safeguard/audit documentation UnifiedCandidateRecord doesn't capture.

Pasal 41-45's independent LVV validation/verification requirement is specific to the domestic Unit Karbon (SRUK) track; there's no normalized 'validated by LVV' field distinct from the raw `dram` passthrough, and reusing Verra's own verra_status here would conflate the domestic and international tracks.
Pasal 54's reporting obligation has no explicit frequency in the rule text itself ('frekuensi tidak disebutkan eksplisit') — nothing to test a specific date against.
Pasal 55(4) binds the Menteri to run an annual review (pihak_terkait: 'Menteri') — never a per-candidate obligation.
Pasal 63's roadmap deadline binds the Menteri, not individual Pelaku Usaha (pihak_terkait says so explicitly) — never applicable to a candidate.
Repeal clause (revokes Permen LHK 7/2023) — not a per-candidate obligation.
Transitional internal registry-operations procedure binding Kementerian Kehutanan internally, not candidates.

Pasal 18 distinguishes SPE GRK recommendation (Menteri Kehutanan's authority) from final SPE GRK issuance (Menteri LH's authority) — two different ministries in one workflow. registration_stage is a single undifferentiated 1-5 progress integer with no field marking which ministry's action is pending.

Pasal 19 classifies the BUYER/counterparty (compliance market vs voluntary market vs public) for a candidate that already holds SPE GRK — about the transaction's counterparty, not the candidate's own registration state. UnifiedCandidateRecord profiles project candidates, not trades, and has no buyer/counterparty field.

Twin of R007 for the DPP track (Pasal 21's 5+5-working-day DPP review SLA) — same blocker as R007: needs the DPP submission timestamp, and `dpp` only carries registration_date/crediting_period dates/methodology (see normalize_verra.py), no submission-date field.

Pasal 22 requires FOUR things together (independent DPP validation, implementation per DPP, independent achievement verification, and a verification report) to support a non-SPE GRK approval request. Verra's own validator/verra_units.issued are evidence from Verra's OWN international process (VCS), not Indonesia's Ministry-level Pasal 22 process — a plausibly-related but different jurisdiction's fact, not the same legal fact. That cross-jurisdiction gap is why this stays unscored here; dossier.py's dpp_validation_proxy surfaces it separately as unscored, hypothesis-tagged, dossier-only evidence (never a badge, never a scoring input) rather than losing the signal entirely.

Twin of R008 for the DPP track (Pasal 23's 14-working-day document-completeness review) — same blocker as R008: needs the non-SPE GRK application submission date, not a normalized field. (Its resulting approval's validity period is governed by R010, already flagged for the same Menteri-approval-date gap.)

Transitional internal registry-operations procedure binding Kementerian Kehutanan internally, not candidates.

Pasal 18 distinguishes SPE GRK recommendation (Menteri Kehutanan's authority) from final SPE GRK issuance (Menteri LH's authority) — two different ministries in one workflow. registration_stage is a single undifferentiated 1-5 progress integer with no field marking which ministry's action is pending.

Pasal 19 classifies the BUYER/counterparty (compliance market vs voluntary market vs public) for a candidate that already holds SPE GRK — about the transaction's counterparty, not the candidate's own registration state. Verra's own validator/verra_units.issued are evidence from Verra's OWN international process (VCS), not Indonesia's Ministry-level Pasal 22 process — a plausibly-related but different jurisdiction's fact, not the same legal fact.
